title: Isothermal titration calorimetry to determine the association constants for a ligand bound simultaneously to two specific protein binding sites with different affinities
protocol: Prepare 300 μL of protein solution by diluting dialyzed protein with buffer Hepes 20 mM (pH 8.0) to a concentration of 50-60 μM.
Prepare approximately 100 μL of ligand solution by diluting the ligand batch solution (50 mM in DMSO) with the dialysis buffer to achieve a concentration ten times that of the protein.
Perform washing cycles of the cell and syringe to avoid interference from contaminants from previous runs.
If necessary, wash the cell with 5% v/v DECON detergent at 60°C for 1 hour followed by abundant water.
Eliminate any trace of methanol from the syringe.
Perform a preliminary experiment with water into water to check baseline stability and ensure the cleanness of the cell and syringe.
Rinse the sample cell with the protein buffer solution.
Fill the sample cell with the protein solution, avoiding bubbles.
Degas all solutions using a vacuum pump or centrifuge to avoid air bubbles during the experiment.
Filter the protein solution to eliminate possible precipitates.
Fill the syringe with the ligand solution.
Perform a couple of purge-refill cycles in the syringe to avoid air bubbles.
Determine very accurately the concentration of the ligand using an analytical balance.
Rinse the surface of the needle with water to eliminate any trace of the ligand.
Wipe the needle with a Kimwipe.
Choose instrument settings for your experiments.

Set 20 injections, initial delay 60 seconds, spacing 180 seconds, filter period 5 seconds, injection volume 2 μL, measurement temperature at 25°C, reference power at 5 μcal s^-1^, and stirring speed at 1000 r.p.m.
Start the experiment after gently setting the syringe in place.
Rerun the ITC assay for reverse titration and titration with the ligand into the protein pre-equilibrated with a second ligand using the same running parameters as in the first titration.
Perform blank experiments titrating the buffer in the cell with the ligand solution.
Correct manually the integration of the peaks after adjusting the baseline to eliminate the effect of bubbles or drifting of the baseline.
Subtract the blank experiment to correct for dilution effects of the ligand in the buffer.
Fit the data using a suitable model such as the One set of sites model.
Evaluate the fitting curve and errors on Ka and enthalpy after fitting.
